thread:
maria: Hey @people-ops — quick heads up: my partner and I are expecting a baby around June 10. I'm planning to start leave ~2 weeks before the due date and take ~12 weeks after. Can someone confirm when I should submit paperwork, which forms are required, how this interacts with short-term disability (STD) and FMLA, and any steps I need to take for coverage (on-call, handoffs)?

jordan: Congrats, maria! :tada: High-level steps: 1) File a parental leave request in the HR portal as soon as you can (we ask for ~30 days notice when foreseeable). 2) If you want job-protected leave, submit the FMLA/CFRA certification (if eligible). 3) For pay: file an STD claim (state or private) — STD typically covers a portion of wages; Redwood has a top-up policy for primary caregivers (details below). 4) Add newborn to medical + flexible savings within 30 days after birth. I'll DM links and checklist.

maria: Thanks — is the 30-day notice a hard requirement? Also what's the top-up look like?

jordan: It's not a hard blocker if birth is earlier/later, but it helps payroll and coverage planning. Top-up policy (summary): Redwood provides 8 weeks paid parental leave at 100% base pay for primary caregivers, paid by payroll (company-paid). After that you can choose to supplement state STD (if applicable) with accrued PTO to reach up to your normal pay for up to 4 additional weeks. If you adopt or are a non-primary caregiver, you get 4 weeks company-paid leave. I'll attach the policy link in a sec.

todd: FYI payroll deadlines: to have company-paid leave reflected in the next monthly paycheck, we need the parental leave request + STD claim submitted at least 10 business days before the payroll cutoff. Payroll cutoff is the 1st of each month for the following month's payroll (so for leave starting June 1, submit by May 18). If you miss that, we can still process but it may hit the following cycle. Also: STD claims often need the attending physician's certification and an official STD form — file that with the insurer right away after you get the due date.

katie: Also adding benefits notes: please add the baby as a dependent in Workday or our benefits portal within 30 days of birth to ensure coverage from day 1. If you're outside the US, some countries have different statutory benefits — ping me and I can check for your location. For adoption, we need placement documentation instead of medical docs. For parental pay coordination: state programs (CA/NY/etc.) may pay a portion; submit both company forms and state claim to avoid gaps.

elaine: Manager perspective: we can prep coverage plan early. maria, can you draft a 1-pager runbook with your weekly cadence, critical PRs, and an on-call handoff? I can reassign two ongoing tickets and move your biggest launch to next sprint. We should also decide if we want a short-term contractor for the 8–12 week window. Happy to cover hiring ops coordination if you want. :+1:

maria: I'll put together the runbook tonight and list transfers. For contractor — yes please, that would help with front-end work. What do I need to include for hiring ops?

elaine: In the hiring req please add: duration (12 weeks), hourly range, skills: React + TS, familiarity with our design system, overlap date with you for onboarding. People Ops, can you advise on the contractor vendor and speed?

jordan: We usually use our vendor bench for 4–16 week contracts. I'll spin up a short hiring ops checklist and intro to vendor contacts. For a contractor start aligned to your last week onsite is ideal (2–3 days overlap for onboarding).

samir: Congrats @maria! If you want someone to pair with for the handoff let me know — I can take the on-call shift for the first two weeks after you go OOO.

maria: Appreciate it, samir — that helps a lot.

hr-bot: AUTOMATED: "Parental leave request received for maria (thread 1719004321). Please upload supporting docs: FMLA/CFRA cert (if applicable), physician's note, STD claim confirmation, and dependent documentation post-birth."

jordan: One more practical tip — for code owners and alerts, add an "on-call escalation" section in your runbook like the snippet below so the team can triage consistently:

```
oncall: 
  primary: pagerduty-team-A
  escalation: eng-sre 
  runbook: "restart model service -> check GPU pool usage -> escalate to runtime oncall"
  contacts: samir, elaine, todd
```

maria: Great, done. Uploaded draft runbook and parental leave request in the portal. Thanks everyone. I'll DM any private docs.

katie: Final note on benefits: don't forget to elect short-term disability and family leave when filing the state claim (some states have both). If you want, I can do a short 20-min walkthrough of the portal tomorrow.

elaine: Thanks team. maria — we'll get this scheduled and sorted. Congrats again! :heart:

maria: Thanks all — appreciate the help :)
